audience.text: Developers who need to generate or modify PowerPoint presentations on a server or in a build pipeline without installing PowerPoint or using COM interop.

capabilities.text: Create new presentations, open existing ones from paths or streams, save to paths or streams, and save subsets of slides.
capabilities.title: Create and edit presentations

capabilities.text: Add, insert, remove, clone, and hide slides; enumerate masters and layouts; and clone masters.
capabilities.title: Slide manipulation

capabilities.text: Support for 187 of 189 ShapeType values including AutoShapes, picture frames, tables, and connectors with z-order reordering.
capabilities.title: Shape rendering

capabilities.text: Text frames, paragraphs, portions with character and paragraph formatting including bold, italic, underline, alignment, bullets, and text-frame properties.
capabilities.title: Text formatting

capabilities.text: Solid, gradient, pattern, picture, and no-fill options for shapes, lines, text portions, and table cells; line properties including width, dash style, and arrowheads.
capabilities.title: Fill and line styling

capabilities.text: Write notes slides with masters, footer text, slide number visibility, and classic comment authors and comments with timestamps.
capabilities.title: Notes and comments

capabilities.text: Write core, extended, and custom document properties to docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml, and docProps/custom.xml.
capabilities.title: Document properties

capabilities.text: Carry through parts the library does not model unchanged during load and save operations.
capabilities.title: Unknown parts preservation

limitations.text: Does not support saving to formats other than .pptx, .ppsx, and .potx; other SaveFormat values raise NotSupportedException.
Does not support charts, animations, transitions, themes, backgrounds, group shapes, or hyperlinks.
Does not write modern threaded comments; only classic comment lists are supported.
Does not include language attributes in generated presentations; PowerPoint uses the authoring machine's default language.
No API to change slide size; new presentations use a fixed 4:3 screen size.
Picture embedding requires reading bytes manually; no overload accepts a file path directly.

problems_solved.text: Enables server-side PowerPoint generation and modification without requiring a native PowerPoint installation or COM dependencies.
Provides a pure .NET implementation that builds the Office Open XML package directly, avoiding native dependencies.
Supports .NET 8 and .NET 10 with no NuGet dependencies, simplifying deployment and reducing attack surface.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Slides.FOSS for .NET is an MIT-licensed .NET library that creates, reads, and edits PowerPoint .pptx presentations by directly building the Office Open XML package without any external dependencies.

uncertainties: Whether the library supports 3-D properties beyond what is listed in the README.
Whether the library supports SmartArt or OLE objects despite the README stating they are not supported.
Whether the library supports macro-enabled presentations (.pptm) despite the README not mentioning them.
Whether the library supports reading presentations with modern threaded comments even if it cannot write them.
Whether the library supports custom slide sizes via undocumented APIs.
Whether the library supports image rendering or conversion to formats like PDF or images despite the README stating it does not.
Whether the library supports animation or transition properties beyond what is explicitly listed.
Whether the library supports background styling beyond what is explicitly listed.

workflows.name: Create presentation from scratch
workflows.text: Instantiate a new Presentation object, add shapes, text, tables, and other elements, then save to a .pptx file using the Save method.

workflows.name: Load and modify existing presentation
workflows.text: Open a .pptx file via a path or Stream, modify slides, shapes, or text, and save the updated presentation.

workflows.name: Install via dotnet CLI
workflows.text: Run dotnet add package Aspose.Slides.FOSS to add the library to a .NET project.
